speaker: Unknown
en: In travel, you book a flight.
zh: 在旅行领域，你预订航班。

speaker: Unknown
en: In e-commerce, you buy a product.
zh: 在电商领域，你购买商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in healthcare, simply booking an appointment can still take weeks.
zh: 但在医疗健康领域，仅仅预约一个号都可能需要数周时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, A16Z general partner Julie Yu sits down with ZocDoc founder and CEO Oliver Karaz to discuss why healthcare scheduling remains so difficult and how AI could change that.
zh: 在本期节目中，A16Z 普通合伙人 Julie Yu 与 ZocDoc 创始人兼 CEO Oliver Karaz 坐下来探讨为什么医疗排班依然如此困难，以及 AI 如何改变这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oliver explains how ZocDoc built the infrastructure to connect patients with doctors across hundreds of scheduling systems and why the company is now making that technology available to AI agents and other platforms.
zh: Oliver 解释了 ZocDoc 如何构建基础设施，将患者与横跨数百个排班系统的医生连接起来，以及公司现在为什么正在把这项技术开放给 AI 智能体和其他平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also discussed ZocDoc's partnership with Gemini, why no single company should own the front door to healthcare, and how better scheduling can help patients see doctors in days rather than weeks.
zh: 他们还讨论了 ZocDoc 与 Gemini 的合作、为什么不应该由任何单一公司掌控医疗健康的前门，以及更好的排班如何帮助患者在几天而不是几周内看上医生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately, what changes when finding and booking the right doctor becomes as easy as booking a flight.
zh: 以及归根结底，当找到并预约合适的医生变得像订机票一样简单时，会发生什么改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am so excited to be here with Oliver Karaz, who is the CEO of ZocDoc.
zh: 我非常激动能和 Oliver Karaz 在这里，他是 ZocDoc 的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oliver and I go way back.
zh: Oliver 和我认识很多年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You and I are kindred spirits and both having tried to solve a lot of similar problems in healthcare over the years and, dare I say, decades almost.
zh: 你和我是志同道合的人，多年来都试图解决医疗健康领域许多类似的问题，甚至可以说，几乎是几十年的问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like we competed at times.
zh: 而且我感觉我们有时还互相竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: We probably should have just partnered with each other, but it's been fun to share notes with you as ZocDoc has continued to evolve.
zh: 我们也许本应该直接彼此合作，但随着 ZocDoc 持续发展，能和你交流心得一直很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And arguably ZocDoc is one of the few companies in health tech that has truly built like a household iconic name for itself.
zh: 可以说，ZocDoc 是医疗科技领域少数几家真正打造出了家喻户晓的标志性品牌的公司之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So huge kudos for doing that.
zh: 所以对做到这一点表示巨大的赞许。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe Oliver, we can start with you just providing the audience with an update.
zh: 也许 Oliver，我们可以从你开始，给听众们提供一个最新情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is ZocDoc today and how has it evolved the most over the last several years that you've been building the business?
zh: ZocDoc 今天是什么，以及在你经营这门生意的过去几年里，它演变最大的地方是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, thank you, Julie.
zh: 好的，谢谢你，Julie。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, it's been decades, but it feels like days and I always enjoyed learning from you.
zh: 事实上，已经过去几十年了，但感觉就像几天一样，我一直很享受向你学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of your listeners will probably think of ZogDog as a destination website where they go and can find a doctor that accepts their insurance and then...
zh: 所以你的很多听众可能会把 ZogDog 想象成一个目的地网站，他们去那里可以找到一位接受他们保险的医生，然后……

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll book an appointment right there and then.
zh: 他们当场就能预约。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's something that we, of course, still do.
zh: 当然，这仍然是我们现在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what is new now is that we take this infrastructure that we have built that enables that marketplace and we make it available to third parties.
zh: 但现在的最新情况是，我们把我们构建的、支撑这个市场的基础设施开放给第三方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So whether you are a payer, you're an AI platform, you have a consumer audience, you can now give them the ability to schedule their adopters seamlessly, no matter where they start the journey.
zh: 所以无论你是支付方、你是 AI 平台、你拥有消费者受众，你现在都可以让他们无缝预约他们的就诊者，无论他们从哪里开始这段旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: The genesis of this conversation actually was you and I just texting each other after I put a tweet out there a few weeks ago saying tongue in cheek that nothing is certain in life except death, taxes, and the provider directory problem.
zh: 这次对话的起因其实是几周前我发了一条推文之后，你和我互相发短信，我半开玩笑地说，人生中没有什么是不确定的，除了死亡、税收和提供者目录问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you and I have both tried to solve this problem from different angles, but it still persists, right?
zh: 而你和我都曾从不同角度尝试解决过这个问题，但它依然存在，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that's part of why I wrote it was...
zh: 我是说，这正是我写那条推文的部分原因……

speaker: Unknown
en: We continue to encounter, whether it's our startup companies who are trying to build in this area and themselves ask the question, like, why hasn't this been solved?
zh: 我们不断遇到这种情况，无论是试图在这个领域创业的初创公司，它们自己也会提出疑问，比如，为什么这个问题还没被解决？

speaker: Unknown
en: Incumbents who also struggle to maintain precise information about who their providers are, who's doing what, who's bookable, who takes what insurance, et cetera.
zh: 还有现有的大公司，它们也难以维护关于它们的提供者是谁、谁在做什么、谁可以预约、接受什么保险等等的精确信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your view on why this problem has persisted?
zh: 你怎么看待为什么这个问题一直存在？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the fundamental incentive that we've failed as an industry to align that you think is the biggest blocker to having a true golden record for every licensed medical practitioner in this country?
zh: 你认为作为整个行业，我们未能对齐的根本性激励是什么，而它是不是让这个国家每一位持照医疗从业者拥有真正的黄金记录的最大阻碍？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think actually the problem is to a large extent solved.
zh: 是的，所以我认为实际上这个问题在很大程度上已经被解决了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we look at what we're doing, we have the ability to schedule into the providers that are connected to us.
zh: 如果我们看看我们在做的事情，我们已经具备向与我们连接的提供者进行排班的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have data that's more than 99% accurate, which compares quite favorably with your average insurance directory.
zh: 我们的数据准确率超过 99%，这与普通的保险目录相比相当有优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason, and the Gordon knot here was actually enabling the transaction.
zh: 而原因，这里的戈耳狄俄斯之结实际上是让交易得以实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you put out a provider directory, frequently you're in the business of publishing the Encyclopedia Britannica, right?
zh: 当你发布一个提供者目录时，你常常是在做出版《大英百科全书》的生意，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're able to really put it out there and present it to patients.
zh: 你能把它发布出去并呈现给患者。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's already out of date.
zh: 但它已经过时了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're constantly chasing the problem.
zh: 你在不断追赶这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you have the transaction, it's much more like Wikipedia, right?
zh: 一旦你有了交易，它就更像维基百科，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Every incremental transaction actually validates the information you have.
zh: 每一笔增量交易实际上都在验证你拥有的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: You make any mistake you make exactly once and then you know what's going in.
zh: 你犯的任何错误你只犯一次，然后你就知道是怎么回事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, of course, as you know, the actual transactability and the ability for a patient to book seamlessly
zh: 当然，如你所知，实际的可交易性以及患者无缝预约的能力

speaker: Unknown
en: It was an extremely hard problem to solve.
zh: 是一个极其难以解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are hundreds of different EHRs.
zh: 这里有数百种不同的 EHR。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's tens of thousands of insurance plans that need to be mapped.
zh: 有数以万计的保险计划需要映射。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are many, many different ways to work in this, different workflows and different practices, different specialties.
zh: 有很多很多不同的处理方式，不同的工作流程、不同的诊所、不同的专科。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns into this Tetris game that we needed to solve.
zh: 它就变成了一个我们需要解开的俄罗斯方块游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it took us 20 years to get to where we are today, that this infrastructure is available for anyone who wants to plug in and to provide that experience for their patients.
zh: 我们花了 20 年才走到今天这个位置，这套基础设施现在对任何想接入并为其患者提供这种体验的人都可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, that's amazing.
zh: 好的，这太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that is a bold claim and I'm so glad that you are confident that we have solved this problem.
zh: 所以这是一个大胆的说法,我很高兴你有信心我们已经解决了这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we actually double-click on that a little bit, Oliver?
zh: 我们能不能真正深入探讨一下这个问题,Oliver?

speaker: Unknown
en: When I think back to the way that we approach this problem at Kairos, we largely, just to abstract out the problem a little bit, there's three buckets of data that matter about a doctor.
zh: 当我回想我们在 Kairos 处理这个问题的方法时,大体上——稍微把问题抽象一下——关于一位医生,有三类重要的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the basic demographic information, who's a doctor, what are they credentialed in, what insurance they take, organizational affiliations, et cetera.
zh: 有基本的身份信息,谁是医生、他们的执业资格是什么、他们接受哪些保险、组织隶属关系等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a second bucket of data, which is their kind of practice data.
zh: 有第二类数据,也就是他们的执业数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do they actually do clinically in practice?
zh: 他们在临床实践中实际做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe even things like who do they refer to or who refers to them, things of that sort.
zh: 甚至可能还有诸如他们把病人转诊给谁、或者谁把病人转诊给他们,诸如此类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the third, which you alluded to already, is what is their actual availability?
zh: 然后是第三类,你已经提到过了,就是他们的实际可预约情况是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means wiring into the source of truth, like scheduling systems and understanding what the capacity of the system is and how to effectively route.
zh: 这意味着要接入事实来源,比如预约系统,并理解系统的容量是多少以及如何有效路由。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you just walk us through, what is the approach?
zh: 你能带我们走一遍,方法是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, do you have to take a unique approach to each of those buckets?
zh: 比如,你是不是要对每一类数据采取不同的方法?

speaker: Unknown
en: Which one is the hardest to solve?
zh: 哪一类最难解决?

speaker: Unknown
en: Where have you had the most success in doing something that you think is novel relative to everyone else who's tried their hand at this problem over the years?
zh: 相对于多年来尝试过这个问题的其他人,你在哪个方面取得的成功最大,做出了你认为新颖的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think problem one is distinct from the others, right?
zh: 是的,我认为问题一和其他两个是不同的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: This is information that doesn't change as often.
zh: 这是那些不经常变化的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where did they go to med school?
zh: 他们上的哪所医学院?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, where is their practice located?
zh: 比如,他们的诊所在哪里?

speaker: Unknown
en: That seems to be the most tractable problem, and that's why most people focus there.
zh: 这似乎是最容易解决的问题,这就是为什么大多数人把注意力集中在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second two problems are related, and you can both extract them from the EHR, but they are very, very difficult to standardize.
zh: 后两个问题是相关的,你既可以从 EHR 中提取它们,但它们非常非常难以标准化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you sort of an idea.
zh: 我给你一个大概的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, you can write integrations to the EHRs, which we do.
zh: 是的,你可以写与 EHR 的集成,我们就是这么做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have them out of the box for 175 different EHRs plus, but then they're being used very differently.
zh: 我们开箱即用支持 175 种以上不同的 EHR,但它们的使用方式千差万别。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you one complete example.
zh: 我给你一个完整的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we first got started, we realized that there was a practice where we constantly got cancellations from the office manager that said that this doctor isn't available at the time we wanted to book the patient into.
zh: 当我们刚起步的时候,我们发现有一个诊所,我们会不断地收到办公室经理的取消通知,说这位医生在我们想给病人预约的时间段没有空。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we couldn't figure out why because the copy of the calendar and the
zh: 而我们搞不清楚为什么,因为我们这边的日历副本和

speaker: Unknown
en: Practice in our company seemed identical.
zh: 我们公司里那份诊所副本看起来是一模一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we brought all the smartest people at DocTalk in a room.
zh: 我们把 DocTalk 所有最聪明的人都叫到一个房间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I brought them pizza.
zh: 我给他们买了披萨。

speaker: Unknown
en: I walked their dogs.
zh: 我帮他们遛狗。

speaker: Unknown
en: They couldn't figure it out.
zh: 他们也搞不明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I sat next to the office manager.
zh: 于是我坐到了办公室经理旁边。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I realized is that sometimes the doctor would walk out and say, hey, I'm out next Friday.
zh: 我意识到的是,有时医生会走出来喊一声,嘿,我下周五不在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the office manager would actually take a post-it note.
zh: 然后办公室经理会真的拿一张便利贴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And attach that to their monitor instead of going into the EHR.
zh: 贴到他们的显示器上,而不是录入 EHR。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, once you know these things are happening, you can solve for that.
zh: 好吧,一旦你知道这些事情在发生,你就能解决它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Math is your friend.
zh: 数学是你的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out that just one example, there were literally 1,000.1% solutions that we had to figure out to make the EHR integration for scheduling truly accurate.
zh: 事实是,仅仅是这一个例子,我们就有字面意义上的 1,000.1% 个解决方案需要搞清楚,才能让用于预约的 EHR 集成真正准确。

speaker: Unknown
en: Several years to do, and I think many folks just got frustrated with this task and we were stubborn enough to persist.
zh: 这花了好几年时间,我想很多人都对这个任务感到沮丧了,而我们足够固执,坚持了下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, we have now gotten enough information about how EHR is actually used to answer question two and three that you laid out based on a single integration into their EHR.
zh: 结果,我们现在已经获得了足够多关于 EHR 实际使用方式的信息,可以基于对其 EHR 的单次集成来回答你提出的第二个和第三个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We used to joke that 3M was our biggest competitor because of Post-it notes.
zh: 我们过去常开玩笑说,3M 是我们最大的竞争对手,因为便利贴。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other kind of unique distinction that ZocDoc has relative to a lot of others in this space is the fact that you've always been consumer aligned.
zh: ZocDoc 相对于这个领域很多其他公司的另一个独特之处在于,你们一直是站在消费者这一边的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to the point I made earlier, you guys are now a household brand.
zh: 按我之前说的观点,你们现在已经成为家喻户晓的品牌了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think consumers do view ZocDoc as a go-to place when they do need a doctor's appointment, as opposed to many companies, including mine, which took much more of a B2B approach and aligned with health systems, provider organizations, et cetera.
zh: 我认为消费者确实把 ZocDoc 当作需要看医生时的首选之地,而不像许多公司——包括我的公司——采取了更偏向 B2B 的路线,与医疗系统、医疗服务提供方组织等等结盟。

speaker: Unknown
en: To what extent do you think that played into your ability to crack this nut?
zh: 你认为这在多大程度上促成了你们攻下这个难题的能力,

speaker: Unknown
en: uniquely and differently and better than others who are going sort of through the system, so to speak.
zh: 独特地、以不同的方式、比其他人更好地,可以说,从系统内部切入?

speaker: Unknown
en: And can you give some examples of maybe where your consumer-driven approach was ultimately the thing that got, you know, providers to change behavior or that helped solve this problem in a unique way?
zh: 你能不能举一些例子,说明你们以消费者为驱动的方法最终在哪些地方促成了医疗服务提供方改变行为,或者以独特的方式帮助解决了这个问题?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think this speaks to the fact that
zh: 是的,我认为这说明了一个事实,

speaker: Unknown
en: We just firmly believe that everything has to start with the patient.
zh: 我们坚定地相信,一切都必须从患者出发。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when the patient wins, everyone wins.
zh: 当患者赢了,所有人都赢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The provider wins, ZocDoc wins.
zh: 医疗服务提供方赢了,ZocDoc 也赢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's a mindset that we brought to the providers we partnered with.
zh: 这就是我们带给合作医疗服务提供方的一种思维方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's interestingly not a mindset that is easily reinforced by a lot of the other software they use.
zh: 有趣的是，他们使用的其他许多软件并不容易强化这种思维方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a general walled garden preference in healthcare frequently.
zh: 在医疗健康领域，普遍存在一种“围墙花园”的偏好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where the idea is that we own the front door to care, that we own the patient.
zh: 也就是说，我们拥有通向医疗服务的“前门”，我们拥有患者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reality is that that's a flawed premise.
zh: 而现实是，这是一个有缺陷的前提。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because healthcare isn't like a building where you lure the patient in and you slam the door shut behind them.
zh: 因为医疗健康不像一栋建筑，你把患者诱进来，然后在他们身后砰地关上门。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a lot more like a city, right?
zh: 它更像一座城市，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And the patient walks the city and depending on what their need is at this current moment, they might knock on different doors.
zh: 患者在这座城市里行走，根据他们当下时刻的需求，他们可能会敲不同的门。

speaker: Unknown
en: They might go to an urgent care center, you know, their kid is sick, or they might look for the most
zh: 他们可能会去紧急护理中心，你知道的，比如孩子生病了，或者他们可能会寻找最

speaker: Unknown
en: Specialized doctor if they have a rare disease or someone who can be there for the journey if they have a chronic condition.
zh: 专科化的医生，如果他们患有罕见病，或者能陪伴整个病程的人，如果他们有慢性病。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you need to acknowledge that you need to open all the doors in order for this to truly work.
zh: 所以你需要承认，你必须打开所有的门，这一切才能真正运转起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you will sort of take learnings that you would never be able to get from a single EHR because you're focused around the problem the way the patient sees it.
zh: 然后你会得到一些你永远无法从单一 EHR 中获得的经验，因为你是围绕患者所看到的问题来聚焦的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, and just to sort of reinforce that somewhat contrarian view, Oliver, I think the notion that no single party should own the front door, and in fact, there is no single front door, we should enable care no matter where the patient wants to go, is somewhat at odds with kind of the belief that I think has been long held by people in the system, which is that if you think about it that way, you might sacrifice some of the coordination that is necessary to ensure that a patient is getting the right care at the right time longitudinally.
zh: 好的，为了再强化一下这个 somewhat 反传统的观点，Oliver，我认为“任何单一方都不应拥有前门，实际上根本不存在单一前门，无论患者想去哪里我们都应该提供医疗服务”这一观点，与系统内的人们长期持有的信念有些相悖，那就是：如果你那样想，你可能会牺牲一些必要的协调，以确保患者在纵向时间线上在正确的时间得到正确的医疗。

speaker: Unknown
en: To a point that they actually resolve whatever health issues that they have.
zh: 直到最后他们真正解决自己所有的健康问题。
